title: Daily X narrative digest — 2026-11-03

hits.name: OpenAI Developers
hits.hook: OpenAI built Pando, a Git backend: ~80% lower push latency, nearly a petabyte of Git data a day
hits.text:
We built Pando, a new Git backend for our monorepo, to handle more pushes and fetches without changing how our engineers and agents use Git.

Pando cut push latency by ~80% and now serves nearly a petabyte of Git data a day. We can grow Git capacity alongside agent usage. https://t.co/4c0YXOfKqK
hits.original:
We built Pando, a new Git backend for our monorepo, to handle more pushes and fetches without changing how our engineers and agents use Git.

Pando cut push latency by ~80% and now serves nearly a petabyte of Git data a day. We can grow Git capacity alongside agent usage. https://t.co/4c0YXOfKqK
hits.draft_en:
OpenAI had to build its own Git backend, Pando, so agents and engineers could keep pushing without slowing down. Push latency is down about 80%, and it now serves nearly a petabyte of Git data a day.

Agents don't just need smarter models, they need sturdier plumbing.

Before you roll out your next Copilot Studio agent, check where it will queue up first: connections, throttling, approvals.
hits.video_tip: Vertical 20s: a simple pipe diagram, agent runs flow in and one narrow section glows red. Zoom in on it and label it 'your connection limits'.

hits.name: OpenAI
hits.hook: OpenAI plans an internal security sprint with Cathedral Systems: defenders should put AI to work first
hits.text:
As AI becomes more capable at finding vulnerabilities, defenders need to put it to work before attackers do.

We’re planning our next internal security sprint at OpenAI and partnering with Cathedral Systems, whose researchers will use our models alongside our teams to challenge

hits.draft_en:
OpenAI says defenders need to put AI to work on vulnerabilities before attackers do, and it's lining up an internal security sprint with outside researchers using its models.

You can run a tiny version of that.

Before your agent goes live, point a second agent at it and ask how it could be misused. Cheap red team, ten minutes, fixes the embarrassing stuff first.
hits.video_tip: Talking head 15s: 'Agent one builds, agent two attacks.' Cut to a split screen where the second agent's findings pop up as sticky notes on the first.

hits.hook: GitHub Copilot publishes data on which models perform best in Copilot, for the first time
hits.text:
We often get asked what the best model is in GitHub Copilot.

Our team spends an enormous amount of time optimizing the GitHub Copilot harness for the best, most token-efficient results.

For the first time, we're publishing our data on what models perform best in Copilot:
hits.original:
We often get asked what the best model is in GitHub Copilot.

Our team spends an enormous amount of time optimizing the GitHub Copilot harness for the best, most token-efficient results.

For the first time, we're publishing our data on what models perform best in Copilot:
hits.draft_en:
GitHub just published its data on which models perform best in Copilot, for the first time. Real numbers beat vibes.

Steal that for your own agents.

Pick two models, run the same ten everyday prompts through your Copilot Studio agent, and keep a score sheet. Your gut feeling is not a benchmark.
hits.video_tip: Screen recording 20s: two agent runs side by side on the same prompt, then a scorecard slides in with a winner ribbon. Caption: 'Receipts, not vibes'.

hits.draft_en:
Tuesday, right?

Open Power Automate, find the flow that failed at 3am, blame the connector.

drafts.text:
OpenAI had to build its own Git backend, Pando, so agents and engineers could keep pushing without slowing down. Push latency is down about 80%, and it now serves nearly a petabyte of Git data a day.

Agents don't just need smarter models, they need sturdier plumbing.

Before you roll out your next Copilot Studio agent, check where it will queue up first: connections, throttling, approvals.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 20s: a simple pipe diagram, agent runs flow in and one narrow section glows red. Zoom in on it and label it 'your connection limits'.

drafts.rides: @pierceboggan Copilot model data (46,044 views) + @OpenAI LifeVal (731,151 views)
drafts.text:
GitHub just published its data on which models perform best in Copilot, for the first time. Real numbers beat vibes.

Steal that for your own agents.

Pick two models, run the same ten everyday prompts through your Copilot Studio agent, and keep a score sheet. Your gut feeling is not a benchmark.
drafts.video_tip: Screen recording 20s: two agent runs side by side on the same prompt, then a scorecard slides in with a winner ribbon. Caption: 'Receipts, not vibes'.

drafts.text:
OpenAI says defenders need to put AI to work on vulnerabilities before attackers do, and it's lining up an internal security sprint with outside researchers using its models.

You can run a tiny version of that.

Before your agent goes live, point a second agent at it and ask how it could be misused. Cheap red team, ten minutes, fixes the embarrassing stuff first.
drafts.video_tip: Talking head 15s: 'Agent one builds, agent two attacks.' Cut to a split screen where the second agent's findings pop up as sticky notes on the first.

drafts.text:
Scott Hanselman is building a GPU Taskman because he couldn't see where his GPU memory was going. That's the best reason to build any tool.

Same with Power Platform.

Your most useful app is usually the ugly one that answers one annoying question. Ship the ugly version this week.
drafts.video_tip: Screencast 15s: a deliberately plain canvas app with one gallery and one button, a 'before: 3 emails, after: 1 click' caption. Keep it shaky and honest.

drafts.text:
Tuesday, right?

Open Power Automate, find the flow that failed at 3am, blame the connector.

It was the connector. It's always the connector. Until it's your own expression, but we don't talk about that.
drafts.video_tip: Meme format 8s: sleepy face, then a run history with a red 'Failed' badge, then a zoom on 'Connector error'. Add a quick 'it was me' caption at the end.
